front: Split conformal recipe in three steps?
back: Fit a model on train data. Compute absolute residuals on a calibration set. Use the ⌈(n+1)(1−α)⌉-th smallest as half-width.
It is a finite-sample correction that makes the coverage guarantee exact for n calibration points.

front: What does conformal need to guarantee coverage?
back: Exchangeability: calibration and new points come from the same process, so their order does not matter.

front: Why do time series break conformal guarantees?
back: Errors are autocorrelated and the world drifts: trend and volatility changes make old residuals too small or too large.
Use only the last W known residuals for each new interval, so the band follows changes in error size.
α(t+1) = α(t) + γ(α − err(t)). A miss lowers α(t), which widens the next interval.
